big: A buyer deducts tax at a high rate when Rohan sells his flat in India. He lives in the UK, where he will pay tax on the same gain. Without a treaty, he could pay twice. With one, he claims credit and pays once.

lines: Will India and my country both tax the same money?
They may, but a treaty called DTAA exists to avoid being taxed twice. You may need a tax residency certificate from your country to claim its benefits.

rows: A treaty between two countries to avoid double tax
Often at higher rates than for residents. Refund possible
From your country, proving you live there for tax
Rent, NRO interest and gains in India. Taxable in India
note: Rules change, so check the current rule with your bank or a qualified adviser.

title: Tax for NRIs
stops: A DTAA helps avoid being taxed twice
TDS on NRIs is always lower than for residents
Rent from an Indian flat is taxable in India
An NRI can never claim a TDS refund
caps: A treaty decides who may tax which income.
TDS rates for NRIs are often higher.
Income arising in India is taxable in India.
An NRI can claim a refund if too much was deducted.

q: Rohan's rent from his Indian flat is paid to him in Dubai. Where is it taxable?
opts: Only in the country of the UAE
Only if he visits India that year
why: It is not tax-free just because he lives abroad.
India has the first claim on Indian-source income.
Tax does not depend on whether he visits that year.
Income arising in India is taxable in India.

q: Meena's TDS on a sale was more than her actual tax. What can she do?
opts: Forget it and move on with life
File a return and claim a refund
Ask her bank to repay the excess
Ask the buyer to return the money
why: Forgetting it leaves her money with the tax office.
A return lets her claim back the excess tax deducted.
The bank cannot refund tax already paid to the tax office.
The buyer already paid the tax over to the government.

q: Rohan applies for treaty benefit. Which document may be asked for?
opts: A shop receipt from a store
why: A shop receipt has no role in treaty claims.
A gym card proves nothing about tax residency.
His country's tax office issues it as proof of residence.
A library card proves nothing about tax residency.

opts: To raise tax in both the countries
To stop all investing across borders
To replace the PAN with a new number
why: A treaty reduces the burden of being taxed in two places.
Its aim is to prevent double tax and not to raise it.
It does not stop investing across borders in any way.
A PAN is still needed in India, whatever the treaty says.

pts: A DTAA helps avoid double tax. Claim it with a residency certificate.
TDS on NRIs is often higher, but excess can be refunded.
Indian-source income is taxable in India.
